# Unit test for function closest_integer
def test_closest_integer():
    # Plain integers
    assert closest_integer("10") == 10
    assert closest_integer("-3") == -3
    assert closest_integer("0") == 0

    # Normal rounding (round half to even via Python's round)
    assert closest_integer("1.4") == 1
    assert closest_integer("1.6") == 2
    assert closest_integer("-1.4") == -1
    assert closest_integer("-1.6") == -2
    assert closest_integer("0.4") == 0
    assert closest_integer("-0.4") == 0

    # Halfway values round away from zero
    assert closest_integer("14.5") == 15
    assert closest_integer("-14.5") == -15
    assert closest_integer("0.5") == 1
    assert closest_integer("-0.5") == -1
    assert closest_integer(".5") == 1
    assert closest_integer("-.5") == -1
    assert closest_integer("2.5") == 3
    assert closest_integer("-2.5") == -3

    # Trailing zeros stripped before deciding
    assert closest_integer("10.0") == 10
    assert closest_integer("10.00") == 10
    assert closest_integer("2.50") == 3      # becomes "2.5" -> away from zero
    assert closest_integer("-2.50") == -3    # becomes "-2.5" -> away from zero
    assert closest_integer("0.00") == 0
    assert closest_integer("-14.50") == -15

    # More decimal cases
    assert closest_integer("15.3") == 15
    assert closest_integer("-15.3") == -15
    assert closest_integer("15.7") == 16
    assert closest_integer("-15.7") == -16

    print("All tests passed!")
